info.title: PoE2 private server API
info.description: Accounts, administration and live log of the private server. Passwords are sent as plain text: use HTTPS outside the local machine.

post.summary: Disables an account: its tokens are revoked and its sessions end.
Enables an account again.
Sets an account's role (`player` or `admin`). You cannot demote yourself.
A `<Server>` chat line to every player.

get.summary: The bans, newest first (history included unless `?active=true`).

parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Only the bans in force now.

post.summary: Lifts a ban that is in force. `404` unknown ban, `409` already over.

get.summary: Characters of all accounts, or of one (`?account=`).
The server's config file, with the form schema.

409.description: not started from a config file

get.summary: The saved previous versions of the config file, newest first.
The text of one backup, to load into the editor.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: backup file name from the list

post.summary:
Writes form values into config text (comments and layout stay) so the editor can show the
result and its diff. Only the keys of the form are accepted; each value is checked against
its type and bounds. Nothing is saved. With an empty `set` it only reads the form values out
of the text (`parse_error` when it does not parse): the editor uses that to fill the form
from text typed in the raw editor.

Saves the text as the server's config file: validates it, keeps a backup of the previous
file and replaces it atomically. `400` with the line and column for an invalid config, `403`
when `[web] config_editor` is off, `409` when the file changed since `base_revision`. With
`restart` the server then restarts like `POST /admin/server/restart`.

Parses the text exactly as the server would at start and reports the first problem with its
line and column, or the warnings of a valid config. Nothing is saved.
Creates an instance without moving anyone into it.
Closes an instance; its players are disconnected.

get.summary:
Live log over WebSocket (upgrade). Server messages are JSON with a `type` of `hello`
(`buffer`), `event` (a `LogEvent`), `reset` (the filter changed, new history follows),
`lagged` (`missed`) or `error`. The client sends a `LogFilter` as JSON text, first and
whenever it changes: `{"min_level":"info","target":"poe_net","text":"kick","history":200}`.

parameters.name: ticket
parameters.description:
A ticket from `POST /admin/logs/ws-ticket`, because browsers cannot set headers on a
WebSocket (the `Authorization` header with the admin's web token works too).

post.summary:
A single-use ticket for the log WebSocket, valid for `[web] web_token_ttl_secs`. Pass it as
`?ticket=` to `GET /admin/logs/ws`; ask again for every connection.

get.summary:
Players, instances, simulation frame time, memory and CPU of the server over time, sampled
every `[metrics] interval_secs` and kept in memory for `[metrics] retention_hours`.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description:
Only samples after this time (unix milliseconds): to fetch what is new since the last
call. Overrides `range_secs`.

parameters.name: range_secs
parameters.description: Only the last this many seconds (default: everything kept).

parameters.name: max_points
parameters.description:
At most this many points (default 600, at most 5000): longer ranges are merged into
buckets that keep the peak of players, instances, memory and frame time.

post.summary:
Sets the message of the day. It takes effect at once (`GET /server`, the launcher's Home
page) and is written into the config file the server runs from (with a backup, like the
config editor); when that is not possible the message still applies until a restart and
`persisted` is false.
Disconnects a player.
Stops a player's chat, for `minutes` or until unmuted.
Moves a player in game to an existing instance (`instance`) or a new one (`area`).
Lets a muted player chat again.

get.summary: The time zone, and every task with its next run and last result.

post.summary: Checks a schedule and lists its next runs, for the form. `400` names the problem.
Creates a task. `400` names what is wrong with the schedule or the options.
Replaces a task's name, action, schedule and enabled flag.
Deletes a task and its history.
Turns a task off; it keeps its history.
Turns a task on; its next run is worked out from now.

400.description: the stored task cannot be read

get.summary: A task's history, newest first (at most 100).

post.summary: Cancels a pending stop or restart while its countdown runs.

409.description: too late: the players were already disconnected

post.summary:
Restarts the server: like stop, then the server starts again (`[server] restart_mode`:
the process starts itself, or exits with code 75 for a supervisor). Web sessions stay valid.

get.summary: The pending stop or restart, if any (with the seconds left).

post.summary:
Stops the server: the players are warned (`delay_secs`, `message`), disconnected, and the
process exits with code 0. Answers 202 at once; the countdown runs on the server.

get.summary:
Players in game now, with their account, character level and class, where they are, since
when, their address and whether they are muted. (The address is only in the admin API.)

post.summary:
Exchanges a launcher token for a fresh `game_remember` token (the client's Remember Me
credential). The launcher writes it into the client's credentials file for auto-login.
post.description:
The game login retires a token when it uses it (rolling tokens), so the launcher token
itself must never be written to the client: it would be revoked by the first game login
and the launcher would be logged out. Only launcher tokens may call this; the new token
lasts `[accounts] remember_days` and does not touch the account's other tokens.

post.summary: Username and password for a token (`kind` `web` by default, or `launcher`).

429.description: too many failed attempts for this account or IP; see the Retry-After header

post.summary: Revokes the token that was used.

get.summary:
The calling account: name, role (`player` or `admin`) and state. For the launcher, to decide
whether to offer "Open web admin" without logging in again. Works with a web or launcher token.

post.summary:
Changes the caller's password. Revokes all of the account's tokens (game logins included)
and returns a fresh token of the same kind as the one used.

429.description: too many failed password attempts; see the Retry-After header

post.summary: Creates a player account (only when `[accounts] open_registration` is on).

get.summary: Server name, version, cluster, players online and where the game client connects.

post.summary:
Exchanges a launcher token for a single-use web sign-in token, so "Open web admin" can open
the browser already logged in. The token lasts `[web] web_token_ttl_secs` (default 60) and
can be redeemed once with `POST /web-token/redeem`; asking again replaces the account's
earlier unused token. Only admins' launcher tokens may call this.

403.description: not a launcher token, or not an admin

503.description: too many unused tokens are waiting

post.summary:
Redeems a web sign-in token for a normal `web` session (12 hours), once. The web admin calls
this from its `#/token-login` page. An unknown, used or expired token gets `401`, all alike.
Failures count against the caller's IP like failed logins (`[security]`): `429` when locked.

401.description: unknown, already used or expired token

429.description: too many failed redeem attempts from this IP; see the Retry-After header

has_password.description: `false` for dev machine-hash accounts: they cannot log in with a password.

BanRequest.description: `POST /admin/bans`: give `account` or `ip`, and optionally how long.

duration_secs.description: Ban length in seconds (60 to 10 years). Neither this nor `expires_at`: permanent.

expires_at.description: End of the ban, unix seconds in the future (instead of `duration_secs`).

ip.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address to ban.

reason.description: Shown to the player (at most 200 characters).

account.description: The owning account's name, when it is known.

area.description: `WorldAreas.Id` of the current or return area.

default.description: The value that applies when the key is absent.

restart.description: Whether a restart is needed for a change to apply.

ConfigFile.description: `GET /admin/config`: the file, its form schema and its warnings.

notices.description: Things to know about this file.

revision.description: Identifies this version of the file: send it back as `base_revision` when saving.

values.description: The values of the form's keys as the file has them (absent: the default applies).

warnings.description: Dangerous settings in the file now (`Config::security_warnings`).

FieldsRequest.description: `POST /admin/config/fields`: form values applied to a text.

content.description: The text to change (the editor's current content).

set.description: `section.key` to the new value; `null` removes the key (the default applies again).

content.description: The text with the values written in; comments and layout are kept.

oneOf.description: Why the text does not parse, if it does not.

values.description:
The form values of that text (as `GET /admin/config` reports them), so the form can be
filled from any text; empty when the text does not parse.

empty_for_secs.description: Seconds since the instance went empty; absent while players are in it.

persistent.description: Towns and hideouts: kept when empty.

topology.description: Forced topology (1-based); absent: the client's choice.

fields.description: The event's other fields, formatted as text.

seq.description: Increases by one per event since the server started.

LogFilter.description: What a client wants to see. Sent as JSON over the WebSocket, first and whenever it changes.

history.description: How many of the newest matching buffered events to send first.

oneOf.description: Events at this severity or worse.

text.description: Only events whose message or fields contain this text (case-insensitive).

LogLevel.description:
Severity, ordered from most severe to most verbose (`Error < Warn < ... < Trace`), so
"at least `min_level`" is `level <= min_level`.

kind.description:
`web` (default, 12 hours) or `launcher` (`[accounts] remember_days`; the game login
also accepts it).

token.description: 64 hex characters: send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Shown only once.

cpu_pct.description:
CPU use of the server process, percent of one core; absent for the first sample and on
platforms where it is unknown.

occupied.description: Instances with at least one player.

rss_bytes.description: Resident memory of the server process in bytes (0: unknown on this platform).

tick_count.description: Simulation frames in the interval, and their mean and longest time in microseconds.

enabled.description: `[metrics] enabled`; when off there are no samples.

motd.description: Plain text, at most 280 characters, line breaks allowed. Empty clears it.

note.description: Why it was not written (config editor off, no file, read-only file, ...).

persisted.description: Whether it was also written into the config file, so it survives a restart.

NewInstanceRequest.description: `POST /admin/instances`, and the `New` form of a transfer.

orientation.description: Forced orientation 0..8; absent: the client's choice.

seed.description: Terrain seed; absent: the server picks one.

topology.description: Forced topology, 1-based in the area's list; absent: the client's choice.

ip.description: The client's address (admin API only), when known.

level.description: Level of the character, when it is in the database.

PendingShutdown.description: A shutdown that was requested and has not happened yet.

cancellable.description: `false` once the final announcement is out: it can no longer be cancelled.

delay_secs.description: The countdown the request asked for.

message.description: The admin's message to the players.

remaining_secs.description: Seconds until the players are disconnected (0 once the final announcement is out).

next_runs.description: The next runs (unix seconds), up to 5.

password.description: Plain text, at least 8 characters. Use HTTPS outside the local machine.

RunView.description: One entry of a task's history.

due_at.description: When the run was scheduled for (unix seconds).

base_revision.description: The `revision` of the file the editor opened.

oneOf.description: Restart the server after saving (the same options as `POST /admin/server/restart`).

backup.description: File name of the backup of the previous version.

changed.description: `false`: the text equals the file, nothing was written.

lines_changed.description: Lines that differ from the previous version.

restart_error.description: Why the requested restart did not start (the file is saved anyway).

oneOf.description: A five-field cron expression: `minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week`.

enabled.description: `[scheduler] enabled`: when off, tasks are listed but never run.

timezone.description: The zone the schedules are in (`Europe/Berlin`, or `UTC+02:00` when it has no name).

utc_offset.description: The zone's offset from UTC now, `+02:00`.

gateway_region.description: Realm region written into the client's gateway list.

instance_port.description:
Port of the instance server the client is sent to (with `login_host`); the launcher
trusts both addresses in the client hook.

login_host.description: Host the game client connects to.

login_port.description: Port the client connects to for login (`[network.login] public_port`, else the bind port).

motd.description:
Message of the day (`[server] motd`, plain text, at most 280 characters); absent when
there is none. The launcher's Home page shows it.

version.description: The game client version this server speaks.

ShutdownKind.description: What the process does once the countdown is over.

delay_secs.description:
Countdown in seconds (0..=3600, default 0): announced to the players in game, then the
server shuts down.

message.description: Added to every announcement (at most 200 characters).

oneOf.description: The requested shutdown that has not happened yet, if any.

TaskBody.description: The body of create and update.

oneOf.description:
Restart the server like `POST /admin/server/restart`: the players are warned during the
countdown, then disconnected, and the server starts again (`[server] restart_mode`).

message.description: Added to every announcement (at most 200 characters).

TaskKind.description: A task's action and its options.

TaskView.description: A task as the page shows it.

next_run_at.description: When it runs next (unix seconds); absent for a disabled task.

oneOf.description: Absent when the stored task cannot be read (`problem` says why).

task_text.description: The task and the schedule in words.

TransferRequest.description:
`POST /admin/players/{name}/transfer`: give `instance`, or `area` (with the optional
layout fields) for a new one.

expires_in_secs.description: Seconds from now until it expires (`[web] web_token_ttl_secs`).

login_path.description:
Where to open the web admin so it signs in with this token: append it to the server's
web address, e.g. `http://host:8080` + `login_path`. The token is in the URL fragment,
so it is not sent to the server, not logged by proxies and not sent as a referrer; the
web admin removes it from the address bar and the history at once.

token.description:
64 hex characters. Single use: redeem it with `POST /web-token/redeem` (the web admin
does this itself when opened through `login_path`). Shown only once; never log it.

expires_in_secs.description: Seconds from now until it expires (`[web] web_token_ttl_secs`).

ticket.description: 64 hex characters, single use: `GET /admin/logs/ws?ticket=<ticket>`. Never log it.

tags.name: admin
tags.description: Admin role and a web token
